metadata.title: API Impact — The Pitch
metadata.author: Chethan Gowda
metadata.audience: hiring managers and engineers hiring for AI software engineering roles
overrides: No Liam / 'in for Bear' persona, no @NikBearBrown chip, no NBB logo bug, no ClaudeTitleOutro (hardcodes @NikBearBrown): the assignment says narrate as yourself, without the instructor's name, persona or credit line.
Voice am_michael instead of the toolkit default am_onyx, so the film is not voiced like the instructor's channel.

Recruiter-facing cut (2026-10-14): no Claude composer cold open and no 'Your turn' handoff. The film is a project pitch for a recruiter, not a Claude walkthrough. Claude appears only as a component of the planned tool.

Scope change (2026-10-14): the tool will also open draft fix PRs in frontend repos (confirmed lines only, must pass tsc + tests, human merges; removed fields reported, not fixed). Problem-first order: B02 opens the film.

beats.narration_text: A backend developer renames one field, username to handle. Tests pass. The pull request merges and ships. Then a profile page in another team's repo goes blank, because it still reads username. Nothing in that pull request could have warned them.

show.event: backend repo card: diff line 'username' struck, 'handle' added
status chips tick: tests pass · merged · deployed
frontend repo card lights: '{{ p.username }}' still reads the old field
profile page mock goes blank — terracotta break mark

beats.narration_text: I'm Chethan. I'm working toward A I software engineering roles, and this is the project I want to build to get there: API Impact.

show.event: 'API Impact.' title with 'Find the frontend lines your API change breaks, and fix them before you merge.'
fact row lands: By · Target role · Status (planned)
synthetic-voice disclosure, bottom right

shot.honesty_label: Status shown as Planned; synthetic narration disclosed on screen

beats.narration_text: The idea: before you merge, API Impact will find the frontend lines your change breaks, and open a fix pull request in each frontend repo, linked to yours.

show.event: writer types 'Before you merge, API Impact will find and fix the specs that break.'
'specs' turns terracotta, is deleted, 'frontend lines' types in

beats.narration_text: Half of this is solved. Tools like O-A-S diff and Optic flag breaking changes in an OpenAPI spec, in C I. They tell you the spec broke. They don't find the frontend lines or fix them, and that's the part that costs a backend developer a broken release.

show.event: three columns: oasdiff · Optic · API Impact (planned)
row 1 'flags breaking spec changes' ticks for all three
row 2 'runs in CI' ticks for all three
row 3 'names the frontend file:line' — dash, dash, 'will' in terracotta box
row 4 'opens a fix PR in the frontend repo' — dash, dash, 'will'

beats.narration_text: Why not just search and replace? A plain search of the public Angular RealWorld frontend for username returns a hundred seventy-one matches, a hundred twenty-four of them in tests. Replace those blindly and you break more than you fix.

show.event: the command types: grep -rnw username src (ts, html)
counter runs to 171 matches · 23 files
bar splits: 124 in *.spec.ts vs 47 elsewhere
real sample lines: formControlName, route param, comment, {{ p.username }}

beats.narration_text: The service fetches a profile, the component stores it, and the template reads p dot username. The object changes names three times before the field is read. API Impact will follow that chain, and touch only those lines.

show.event: profile.service.ts:19-20 — http.get('/profiles/') + map(data => data.profile)
profile.component.ts:54-55 — subscribe(([profile, user]) …) · profile.set(profile)
profile.component.html:11,17 — @if (profile(); as p) · {{ p.username }}
terracotta link draws through all three: call → response → variable → property

beats.narration_text: Here's how it will work. O-A-S diff will find the break, tree-sitter will trace each field to where it's read, and Claude will handle what static analysis can't settle, in a fixed format, and draft the edits. Then it will open draft pull requests.

show.event: stage 1 oasdiff lights
stage 2 tree-sitter trace lights
stage 3 Claude (hard cases only) lights, 'fixed JSON contract' tag
stage 4 verify lights
stage 5 Draft PRs lights

beats.narration_text: The part I care about most: nothing is trusted on the model's word. Every line Claude points to will be re-checked, and every fix must pass that frontend's own tests before a pull request opens. The model suggests; the code decides.

show.event: three citations enter, tagged confirmed / possible / cited
confirmed line: has field ✓, fix passes tsc + tests ✓ → FIX PR
possible line: has field ✓, no fix attempted → LIST ONLY
line without 'username' → struck, DROPPED

beats.narration_text: Here's what that will look like, as a mock-up: a draft pull request in the frontend repo, linked to the backend change, with the edit and its checks. Possible matches will be listed, not edited, and nothing will merge without a human.

show.event: draft PR card: 'Rename username → handle', opened from the backend PR
diff: − {{ p.username }} / + {{ p.handle }}
checks: tsc ✓ tests ✓ · waiting for human review
'Listed, not edited: follow-button.component.ts:34 (possible)'
Merge card: nothing auto-merges

shot.honesty_label: CONSTRUCTED — mock-up of a v1 draft fix PR

beats.narration_text: I'll test it on forked RealWorld repos with about twenty planted breaks, measuring catches, false alarms, citation accuracy and fixes that pass tests, against plain search and a type-check baseline. No results yet, so no numbers here. If they hold up, they'll show I can ground a model in real code, verify its output, and evaluate it. Not agent loops: this is a pipeline.

show.event: test bed card
grid: 3 metrics × 3 systems, every cell 'no result yet'
row 4 'fixes passing tests' — n/a for baselines
skill chips: source grounding · verification · prompt contracts · evaluation · agent loops — not claimed

beats.narration_text: Version one stays narrow: renamed or retyped fields, in TypeScript frontends. It will never merge its own fixes, and it won't guess at deleted fields. It will flag those instead. The first thing I'll get running is one planted rename. You'll know it worked when it prints the exact line, and its draft fix passes C I.

show.event: WILL HANDLE: renamed fields · retyped fields · TypeScript frontends
WILL NEVER: merge its own fixes · guess at deleted fields (flags them) · GraphQL (v1)
RUNS FIRST: one planted rename → exact file:line → draft fix passes CI
'That's how you'll know it ran' check

beats.narration_text: The real risk is a fix that compiles but is wrong, like a username from a different endpoint. So only confirmed lines get edited, fixes must pass the tests, and a human merges. If tracing doesn't hold up on real Angular code, I'll narrow the scope and say so.

show.event: risk card: a fix that compiles but is wrong
guardrails list ticks in
fallback card: narrow v1 if tracing doesn't hold up

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's mostly learning. I come from Angular and TypeScript, so I know the code on the receiving end, though none of that work is public yet. New to me: tree-sitter, O-A-S diff, GitHub Actions, Claude's structured output, and evaluating an A I that edits code.

show.event: left: ALREADY HAVE — Angular · TypeScript (tag: experience, not public yet)
right: NEW TO ME — six chips land one by one
bridge arrow frontend → backend

beats.narration_text: Today, there's this plan and this video. When it's built, it will be a public repo with a GitHub Action and a command-line tool. In the first minute, a hiring manager will see a real draft fix from the test bed, then the eval report.
